newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - October 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - October 11.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Friday.
- Representatives of Loyalist paramiliary organisations are expected to meet in Belfast on Friday to make a formal decision on the future of their ceasefire.
- The government is to set up a personal injuries tribunal in an effort to reduce spiralling insurance costs by up to 50 million Irish pounds a year.

- Gavin O'Reilly, son of businessman Tony O'Reilly, has paid 1.95 million Irish pounds for a period mansion in Dalkey, County Dublin, the highest price ever paid for a private Irish residence at auction.
- Sources close to the Central Bank have warned that budget policy needs to be tightened to ward off inflation and ensure Ireland meets the price criteria in the Maastricht Treaty.

- Esat Digifone, which holds Ireland's second mobile phone franchise, is close to having 80 percent national coverage for its telecommunications signals but is unlikely to launch its service before Christmas.
- British prime minister John Major will attempt to breathe new life into the Northern Ireland talks process when he addresses the Conservative Party conference in Bournemouth on Friday.
- Personal injury claims from motoring or workplace accidents should be heard by an independent tribunal rather than the courts, a report commissioned by the government says.
- A global debt collection firm, believed to be the first of its kind, is to set up business this December in the International Financial Services Centre (IFSC).

- Fianna Fail leader Bertie Ahern told the joint business council of the Irish Business and Employers' Confederation that his party was conducting a detailed analysis of the semi-state and state-sponsored sector and its potential for the future.
